paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God made the first move, and He made it while we were at our worst. Paul says Christ died for the ungodly "while we were still powerless" (Romans 5:6), and "While we were still sinners, Christ died for us" (Romans 5:8). Nobody cleaned up first. Nobody sent a résumé. I've seen a lot of folks try to earn their way in, and I was the guy who ended up in a junk drawer, so trust me, God's love doesn't wait for us to get it together.

That's why Paul can say we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 5:1). We were enemies, and now we're reconciled, and the only thing that changed the story was the death of His Son (Romans 5:10). So the peace isn't a mood you have to work up. It's a standing you've been given, and the grace we stand in is something we've gained access to by faith (Romans 5:2). That means you can stop trying to be good enough and start resting in what Jesus already did.

And here's the part that gets me, friend. If God did the hardest thing for enemies, how much more will He keep us now that we're His? Paul says it twice: "how much more shall we be saved" (Romans 5:9, 10). So when suffering shows up, you don't have to panic, because hope "does not disappoint us, because God has poured out His love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit" (Romans 5:5). Rejoice in God, baker. You're not hanging on by your fingernails, you're held.
